newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: 37 ethnic Albanians reported arrested in Kosovo.
newsitem.headline: 37 ethnic Albanians reported arrested in Kosovo.

text.p: Thirty-seven ethnic Albanians have been arrested so far this week in the Serbian-ruled province of Kosovo and more detentions were likely, the region's mainstream political leader said on Friday.

Ibrahim Rugova, head of the main ethnic Albanian political party, the Democratic League of Kosovo, told a news briefing in the provincial capital Pristina the arrests were tantamount to a "major provocation" by Serbian authorities.

"Since 26 January the Serbian police has engaged in a severe campaign of violence and arrests of Albanian political and human rights activists, but also students and teachers," Rugova said in remarks reported by his party and faxed to Reuters in the Serbian capital, Belgrade.
Kosovo has long been regarded by Western political analysts as a tinder box of communal tensions which, if ignited, could plunge the Balkans into another paroxysm of sectarian warfare.
No comment was available from the Serbian government, already under pressure from widening dissent among Serbian students, opposition parties and professional groups.

Kosovo's ethnic Albanian majority has been careful to distance itself from the Serbian protests for fear of becoming a scapegoat for the increasingly beleaguered government of Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic.
Several Albanian and Serbian lives have been lost over the past year in a shadowy war fought by guerrillas of the little-known Liberation Army of Kosovo.

Rugova's Democratic League says this week's police raids were carried out on the pretext of searching for "terrorist" arms. Some people had been released, Rugova said, including local Red Cross official Qerim Spahiu but others were still being sought by Serbian police.
In 1989, Milosevic cancelled Kosovo's status as an autonomous region on the grounds that the Albanian population was preparing to secede.

Rugova said the campaign of police raids "represents one of the greatest provocations that Kosovo has been exposed to" and he appealed to the international community to help prevent Kosovo from being "engulfed in a spiral of violence."
